Free · Open source · Project-based

Learn French, from zero to TCF Canada

Zéro French is a free, open-source curriculum for passing the TCF Canada. Written lessons, the best free resources on the internet, and a practice project every few lessons to build real fluency.

Start with A1 Basics How it works

3 paths · 44 lessons · 8 practice projects

The curriculum

  1. 00

    A1 Basics

    Start from zero: learn the French alphabet, pronunciation, greetings, basic grammar and everyday vocabulary.

    20 lessons · 4 projects
    ~100 hours
  2. 01

    A2 Survival French

    Handle day-to-day interactions: narrate past events, ask detailed questions, navigate housing and transport, and communicate with public services.

    20 lessons · 4 projects
    ~100 hours
  3. 02

    B1 Independent French

    Achieve functional autonomy: express nuanced opinions, formulate hypotheses, negotiate professionally, and master the subjunctive mood.

    4 lessons · 0 projects
    ~200 hours

Who it's for

  • Express Entry applicants

    Need NCLC 7+ in French to maximise CRS points for permanent residency.

  • PNP candidates

    Many Provincial Nominee Programs award extra points or require a minimum French level.

  • Citizenship applicants

    Need to demonstrate adequate French (or English) proficiency for Canadian citizenship.

  • Complete beginners

    The A1 path starts from zero — no prior French knowledge required.

Frequently asked questions

Is Zéro French really free?

Yes. Every lesson is free, and every linked resource is free to use. The only optional cost is a few dollars for premium practice tools, but free alternatives exist for everything.

Do I need any French experience to start?

No. The A1 Basics path starts from zero: the French alphabet, pronunciation, greetings and basic sentence structure. If you already have some French, use the placement guide to find your level.

How long does it take to finish?

The full curriculum covers roughly 600 hours of study, about 10 to 14 months at 10 to 15 hours a week. Your pace will depend on your starting level and the NCLC score you need.

What is the TCF Canada?

The Test de connaissance du français pour le Canada is an official French proficiency test accepted by IRCC for Canadian immigration (Express Entry, PNP, citizenship). It tests listening, reading, writing and speaking.

How is Zéro French different from a course or an app?

It follows the method of The Odin Project: one ordered path, written lessons that link the best free material instead of recording new lectures, and a practice project every few lessons that builds real-world skills.

Zéro French is free and open source, inspired by The Odin Project (not affiliated). Found a broken link or a better resource? Contribute on GitHub.
